item.title: 'Win against India damaged us a lot': Yousuf explains Pakistan cricket's decline
item.description: Pakistan had never beaten India in a World Cup before that match in 2021. Babar Azam scored an unbeaten 68, while Mohammad Rizwan made 79 not out as Pakistan chased down 152 without losing a wicket. The win was celebrated as a historic moment for Pakistan cricket. However, Yousuf believes the victory also changed the mindset of the players and played a role in the team's decline in the years that followed.

item.title: Tech CEO added to FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters list after fleeing from United States
item.description: Tech CEO Bernhard Fritsch has achieved infamy by landing a spot on the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters list after his conviction for investment fraud. Sentenced to fifteen years in prison and required to make restitution, he managed to evade authorities post-arrest in Mexico by escaping to Germany. The FBI is now urgently seeking tips that could lead to his recapture and subsequent conviction.

item.description: MacKenzie Scott has now donated over one billion dollars to historically Black colleges. Her recent forty-two million dollar gift to Elizabeth City State University marked this milestone. Scott has provided significant funding to numerous institutions since 2020. These unrestricted donations empower universities to allocate funds as needed. Her extensive philanthropic efforts support various educational and community initiatives.

item.title: Ultra-rich pay $650,000 for Martha’s Vineyard 'beach keys'
item.description: Exclusive access to beaches on Martha's Vineyard is proving to be a hot commodity, with keys selling for exorbitant amounts—often in the hundreds of thousands. These keys offer private shorelines away from the crowded tourist spots, appealing to affluent buyers. The rising demand pushes prices higher, leaving locals and seasonal renters feeling alienated and resentful over their dwindling access to the island’s natural beauty.

item.title: The Yamuna is rising again: How prepared is Delhi for another flood?
item.description: Delhi is under the shadow of recurrent flooding threats as the Yamuna River inches closer to its danger threshold. The catastrophic floods from the previous year resulted in the displacement of thousands and interrupted vital public services. Fortunately, this year has seen reduced upstream water releases, offering a brief respite; however, the risk of heavy rainfall above could still ignite a serious crisis.

item.title: India eyes nuclear power in Andamans as China challenge grows near Malacca Strait
item.description: Scientists are currently evaluating potential locations for Small Modular Reactors throughout the archipelago. This pivotal initiative is designed to bolster the islands' energy resilience and satisfy increasing energy demands. Additionally, it supports critical infrastructure developments, including the International Container Transhipment Terminal, while further enhancing India's strategic role in the eastern Indian Ocean and its oversight of vital shipping lanes.

item.title: 100% recycled glass foam supports added lanes on Arizona's I-17
item.description: In a groundbreaking interstate expansion project in Arizona, engineers harnessed recycled glass aggregate as a revolutionary structural fill. This eco-friendly innovation not only provided lightweight support for drainage culverts but also showcased impressive compressive strength. Utilizing foam glass from recycled bottles minimized the need for expensive culvert replacements and significantly cut down on construction delays, ultimately transforming waste into vital infrastructure enhancements.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: After reconnection, Lake Erie wetland logged 3.44 million fish detections
item.description: A rejuvenated wetland at Lake Erie witnessed an influx of aquatic wildlife thanks to its reconnection. High-resolution sonar has captured a staggering 3.4 million fish movements entering and exiting this newly transformed habitat. This research reveals valuable insights into how aquatic species engage with restored coastal ecosystems, as fish showcased varied activity throughout both day and night, influencing management strategies for restoring Great Lakes wetlands.

item.title: US war veteran's home threatened by Elon Musk's AI data centre in Tennessee
item.description: Residents in Memphis are grappling with the effects of a massive artificial intelligence data center that has recently opened its doors. The surge in energy consumption has led to soaring utility bills for local families, casting a shadow on community wellbeing. Amidst growing noise pollution and escalating living costs, citizens are voicing concerns about the sustainability of such rapid technological advancements and their impact on daily life.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Hulk Hogan's Florida mansion gets another $1m cut, now listed for $6.9m
item.description: Hulk Hogan’s Clearwater Beach mansion has received another $1 million price cut and is now listed for $6.9 million. The wrestler’s five-bedroom waterfront home was initially listed for $10.98 million after his death. Hogan bought the property for $3.33 million in 2012, while his neighbouring property was purchased for $1.6 million four years later.

item.title: Newlywed stabbed to death by sister-in-law over remark on jailed brother
item.description: A newlywed woman has been tragically murdered, allegedly at the hands of her sister-in-law after a violent argument. The accused is said to have stabbed the victim and hidden her remains in a water tank. This incident stemmed from an earlier quarrel related to the sister-in-law's brother. Following the incident, police utilized CCTV evidence and forensic fingerprints to arrest the suspect, highlighting the dark tensions surrounding the victim's recent marriage.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: How discarded Christmas trees are being used to build dunes on a UK beach
item.description: Discarded Christmas trees are being used to strengthen the sand dunes at St Annes beach on England’s Fylde Coast. Since the project began in 2013, the trees have helped trap wind-blown sand and expand the dunes. The wider dunes act as a natural sea defence, helping protect nearby homes and businesses from coastal flooding while also creating habitat for specialised plants and wildlife.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Charles Leclerc's Ferrari wrecked in brutal Monza crash - Watch
item.description: At Monza, Charles Leclerc experienced a severe crash that halted the race with a red flag, disrupting Ferrari's home grand prix. Fortunately, he emerged from his wrecked car unscathed. After a restart led by George Russell, Kimi Antonelli impressively raced to victory from a lower starting position, while Lewis Hamilton secured sixth place for Ferrari, rounding off their efforts in the race.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: IPO rush ahead: 11 companies line up to raise Rs 7,055 crore from investors
item.description: The primary market in India is gearing up for an exciting week ahead, with eleven main-board IPOs lined up to collectively raise more than seven thousand crore rupees. These IPOs span various sectors, showcasing a vibrant market landscape. Most will launch on Tuesday and Wednesday, highlighting the robust corporate belief and strong liquidity present in the market.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Bullion markets this week: US inflation, crude and Middle East tensions to set the tone
item.description: This week sees potential volatility in gold and silver prices, primarily driven by upcoming US inflation figures and interest rate speculation. The influence of crude oil fluctuations and geopolitical developments in the Middle East also play a significant role. Additionally, ongoing purchases by central banks, notably in China, bolster gold values. Key economic reports from Germany, China, and the Eurozone will further guide market sentiment.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Jaguar Land Rover may cut 4,000 jobs as it targets £1.7bn in savings
item.description: Jaguar Land Rover may cut up to 4,000 jobs as the Tata-owned carmaker targets £1.7bn in savings over two years and seeks to lower its break-even point to 300,000 vehicles. The move comes a year after a major cyberattack disrupted production and could put further pressure on Andy Burnham’s pledge to reindustrialise Britain.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: US envoys in Kyiv, but Russian strikes persist across Ukraine: 8 killed, 69 injured
item.description: Russia ramped up its aerial bombardment across Ukraine, resulting in eight fatalities and sixty-nine injuries. Ukrainian air defense successfully intercepted the majority of the one hundred eight drones launched overnight. Meanwhile, US diplomats arrived in Kyiv for discussions following a meeting with President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Although temporary pauses in attacks were noted over Moscow and Kyiv, broader hostilities persisted in the regions despite ongoing diplomatic negotiations.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Fire Island glass house gets $1.255m price cut but still seeks record $3.995m
item.description: Crest House, a four-bedroom glass estate in Fire Island’s Cherry Grove, has drawn more than 350 viewers since being listed for $5.25 million in July 2026. Despite the attention, the property has not found a buyer. Its price was first cut to $4.85 million and has now fallen to $3.995 million. The current asking price is still far above Cherry Grove’s record sale of $2.7 million.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: Florida island bought for $14.5m in 2015 now asks $89m after major upgrades
item.description: Mark Pentecost has listed his stunning private island retreat for a staggering eighty-nine million dollars. Acquired eleven years ago for a mere fourteen point five million, this one hundred four-acre island boasts a private golf course and twenty-nine potential residential plots. As the founder of It Works!, Pentecost has skillfully developed this paradise into both a business and family haven, offering unparalleled fishing and coastal access near Boca Grande.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Honeytrap, Rs 1 cr demand: Cops probe UP officer’s 'blackmail' before suicide
item.description: A police officer died by suicide after alleged blackmail by a woman and her associates. The woman, her father, and a lawyer were arrested and sent to judicial custody. Investigators claim the woman used recorded conversations to extort money from men. Police suspect the officer was a target of this alleged extortion network. The investigation continues to establish the full sequence of events and financial transactions.
item.dc:creator: PATHIKRIT CHAKRABORTY
